page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, backed by dedicated CPU allocation. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, requiring network-attached storage for persistent data.

Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%, and achieves average scores in single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench single-core evaluations. However, multi-core performance is limited, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read and write speeds categorized as weak to poor.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c2d-highcpu-2 offers a low-cost entry point into dedicated AMD EPYC hardware, though its low memory-to-vCPU ratio and weak multi-core scaling present clear resource density tradeoffs. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded compute tasks, basic web serving, or simple text processing pipelines. It is not recommended for memory-intensive databases, parallel compilation, or heavy multi-threaded workloads due to its poor multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmark results.
